classification.difficultyReason: Combines algebraic angle expressions, special quadrilateral properties, reflex angles, diagonals and several angle relationships.

content.prompt: Determine the value of these pronumerals using your angle relationships knowledge.

spec.description: Connected left triangle and right quadrilateral sharing one vertex, with all four sectors at that vertex retained.
spec.mathematics: Triangle angles 3f, 3f and 2f; quadrilateral angles 90°, h+40, h and 90°; the two remaining sectors at the shared vertex are g and 115°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels are visible.

answer.worked:
Angle sum of a quadrilateral:
$$\begin{align*}90+(h+40)+h+90&=360\\2h+220&=360\\2h&=140\\h&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}3f+3f+2f&=180\\8f&=180\\f&=22.5^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles at a point:
$$\begin{align*}g+90+115+2(22.5)&=360\\g+250&=360\\g&=110^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Quadrilateral with an arc and algebraic label at each interior angle.
spec.answerVisibility: The value of x is hidden.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle with single matching side ticks and three angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: The sides from the bottom vertex to the two upper vertices are equal. The upper angles are 5y−5 and 3y+25; the bottom angle is z.
spec.answerVisibility: The values of y and z are hidden.

answer.worked:
Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal:
$$\begin{align*}5y-5&=3y+25\\2y&=30\\y&=15\end{align*}$$
Each base angle is $5(15)-5=70^\circ$.
Angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}z+70+70&=180\\z+140&=180\\z&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Left-to-right kite with single and double matching side ticks, a right-side extension and two reflex exterior angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: The exterior reflex angle at the left vertex is 250°. The exterior angle between the upper-right side and the extension of the lower-right side is 140°. The bottom reflex exterior angle is x°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the exterior angle givens and x° appear.

answer.worked:
The left interior angle is $360^\circ-250^\circ=110^\circ$ (angles at a point). The right interior angle is $180^\circ-140^\circ=40^\circ$ (angles on a straight line).
The other two interior angles of the kite are equal. Let each be $b$.
$$\begin{align*}110+40+b+b&=360\\2b+150&=360\\2b&=210\\b&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$
The required reflex angle is $x=360^\circ-105^\circ=255^\circ$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral divided by a red dashed diagonal, with equal upper sides and a whole-angle arc crossing the diagonal at the right vertex.
spec.mathematics: The upper isosceles triangle has vertex angle 100°. The left lower angle is 70°. The whole right interior angle is 70°. The lower-left angle is x°.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived 40° or 30° angles are supplied.

answer.worked:
The upper triangle is isosceles, so each base angle is
$$\frac{180^\circ-100^\circ}{2}=40^\circ.$$
The angle below the diagonal at the right vertex is $70^\circ-40^\circ=30^\circ$.
Angle sum of the lower triangle:
$$\begin{align*}x+70+30&=180\\x+100&=180\\x&=80^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Concave quadrilateral with crossed extensions below the lower vertex, a 20° leader, a reflex 330° angle at the upper-right vertex and x° in the smaller notch angle.
spec.mathematics: The upper-left interior angle is 20°, the upper-right reflex exterior angle is 330°, and the angle vertically opposite the lower interior angle is 65°. The concave interior angle is 360°−x°.
spec.answerVisibility: x labels the smaller angle above the notch; no derived interior angle is visible.

answer.worked:
The upper-right interior angle is $360^\circ-330^\circ=30^\circ$ (angles at a point). The lower interior angle is $65^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).
The reflex interior angle at the notch is $360^\circ-x$.
Angle sum of a quadrilateral:
$$\begin{align*}20+30+65+(360-x)&=360\\475-x&=360\\115-x&=0\\x&=115^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Trapezium with matching parallel arrows on its horizontal sides and a red dashed diagonal from upper-left to lower-right.
spec.mathematics: The upper-left interior angle is split into x° and 71°. The lower-left interior angle is 72°.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles between parallel lines sum to $180^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}(x+71)+72&=180\\x+143&=180\\x&=37^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Slanted rhombus with double ticks on all sides, two red dashed diagonals and an external x° leader pointing to the upper-left half-angle.
spec.mathematics: The lower-left angle between its left side and diagonal is 62°. x° is between the upper-left vertex's left side and the other diagonal.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived full angles or diagonal-intersection right angle are added.

answer.worked:
Diagonals of a rhombus bisect its vertex angles, so the lower-left interior angle is $2\times62^\circ=124^\circ$.
Adjacent angles of a rhombus are supplementary, so the upper-left interior angle is $180^\circ-124^\circ=56^\circ$.
Its diagonal bisects that angle:
$$x=\frac{56^\circ}{2}=28^\circ.$$

spec.description: Kite with single left-side ticks, double right-side ticks, both red dashed diagonals, whole-angle arcs at the left and bottom vertices and a top-right half-angle arc.
spec.mathematics: The whole left interior angle is 100°. The angle between the top-to-bottom diagonal and the upper-right side is 71°. x° denotes the whole bottom interior angle.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived 40° or 111° labels are supplied.

answer.worked:
The left triangle is isosceles, so each base angle is
$$\frac{180^\circ-100^\circ}{2}=40^\circ.$$
The right triangle is isosceles, so its bottom base angle equals its top base angle, $71^\circ$.
The whole bottom angle is
$$x=40^\circ+71^\circ=111^\circ.$$
